VERDICT: REJECT

The proposed answer of 4 is not supported. The cited sources look invented: I know of no Huybrechts or Griffiths paper with this title or result. The claimed argument, that the Euler characteristic of a fiber bundle forces exactly four pencils, is also asserted without justification. The "moduli space is irreducible, so the count is constant" step is likewise unjustified.

From my recollection of the literature on surfaces with $p_g = K^2 = 1$ and genus 2 pencils (Catanese and others), the locus admitting a genus 2 pencil is irreducible, and a general member has exactly two such pencils, not four. I am not certain of this, and I could not check the source here.

CONFIDENCE: 3
